dialogues.speaker: Vile
dialogues.text: Huh? Why are you visiting me at this hour... not trying to buy intel from me, are you?

dialogues.speaker: Vile
dialogues.text: I've been very busy lately, you know. A major client has booked two full weeks of my time.

response.speaker: Vile
response.text: Yes. I can't disclose any details, but suffice to say he's exceptionally rich — so don't even think about trying to out-bid him.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, but... shouldn't informants only share their intel with one person?

response.speaker: Vile
response.text: Maybe in an ideal world, but business is business at the end of the day, and if you only have one partnership, you'll eventually starve to death.

response.speaker: Vile
response.text: The Knights of Favonius are sticklers for principle, but even they have a practice of obtaining intelligence from a minimum of two sources during large-scale operations.

response.speaker: Vile
response.text: They've suffered badly from incomplete intelligence in the past. That's why people like me are so important — I'm there when they need the extra support, and I'm free to find other work when they don't.

response.speaker: Vile
response.text: Here's an analogy. Imagine the Abyss Order has set up an ambush in the wilderness — a single scouting team is unlikely to detect it.

response.speaker: Vile
response.text: Next thing you know, a knight on patrol passes by, completely unsuspecting, when suddenly "Waah!" A monster jumps out and clubs him over the head with a "bish" and a "bash."

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...Why the sound effects?

response.speaker: Vile
response.text: Well, I just thought they might make the whole thing sound more realistic.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Nope, not even close! Monsters go "Yaah!" not "Waah!" And it's a "swish" and a "smash," not a "bish" and a "bash"!

response.speaker: Vile
response.text: Don't be so single-minded... You can think what you want, of course, but it can't hurt to keep my version on file as alternative intel.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Hmm, guess that kinda makes sense...

response.speaker: Vile
response.text: Anyway, to get back to the point... buyers are demanding multiple sources, and it's only fair that informants are free to serve multiple clients too, don't you think?

response.speaker: Vile
response.text: Of course I do. All work is just selling your labor hours. The intelligence business is no different.

dialogues.speaker: Vile
dialogues.text: Still she refuses to admit it, despite being confronted with all the evidence...

dialogues.speaker: Vile
dialogues.text: Oh, it's you, Traveler.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What were you muttering to yourself about?

dialogues.speaker: Vile
dialogues.text: Sara decided she wanted to import Liyue chili peppers recently. Allegedly, they're hot enough to reduce even Mondstadt's die-hard spice lover Barbara to tears.

dialogues.speaker: Vile
dialogues.text: My view is they'd be nigh on impossible to sell, seeing as eighty-six percent of Mondstadters won't touch them.

response.speaker: Vile
response.text: Oh, you hadn't heard? It was my understanding that everyone in Mondstadt knew.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Tell me some more things that everyone in Mondstadt knows.

response.speaker: Vile
response.text: Things like when Outrider Amber volunteered to cook at the last Knights of Favonius get-together, burnt the steak, and smoked out the whole kitchen?

response.speaker: Vile
response.text: Even though Amber made everyone there promise to never tell a soul...

response.speaker: Vile
response.text: ...I think you might be the last person in Mondstadt to hear about it.

choices.text: You should tell her about your concerns.

response.speaker: Vile
response.text: Oh believe me, I've tried.

response.speaker: Vile
response.text: If I can't think of anything better, I may have to send in Prince Charming...

response.speaker: Vile
response.text: Kaeya's got a certain way with words. He would only need to drop a few subtle hints and the whole thing would be sorted.

response.speaker: Vile
response.text: Ahem. Anyway. Thanks for the chat.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Vile
dialogues.text: See you soon.

dialogues.speaker: Vile
dialogues.text: If you hear any funny stories on your travels, do share!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What were you muttering to yourself about?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Tell me some more things that everyone in Mondstadt knows.

response.speaker: Vile
response.text: Certainly, I'm sure everyone knows about Librarian Lisa's habit of drinking afternoon tea.

response.speaker: Vile
response.text: Well, one day, a traveling merchant from Liyue saw Lisa using some special web-shaped things to filter her tea.

response.speaker: Vile
response.text: Although the merchant never saw exactly what it was that Lisa was using, nevertheless a new drink known as Earl Stocking Tea was later released imitating Lisa's own technique.

response.speaker: Vile
response.text: Shortly after the matter, some people claimed that what Lisa was using for her tea was just an ordinary filtration material, used all the time in alchemy. But even I'm not entirely sure what the truth of the matter is...

response.speaker: Vile
response.text: Over time, that ambiguously named tea drink started to gain popularity, even in Mondstadt, a city that's known for its wine culture more than anything else.

response.speaker: Vile
response.text: I can't help but admire the entrepreneurial minds of the people of Liyue. They're always coming up with something bound to catch on with people... Hmm...

response.text: Tell me some more things that everyone in Mondstadt knows.

response.speaker: Vile
response.text: Sure. Besides for just political purposes, they say that merchants were also among the diplomatic mission that came to Mondstadt from Snezhnaya. They came bearing "Fire-Water," a kind of specialty alcohol from Snezhnaya, with aims of starting a partnership with Dawn Winery.

response.speaker: Vile
response.text: During the banquet that was held at Dawn Winery, Master Diluc raised his glass filled with the exotic Snezhnaya Fire-Water and asked a maid to fill the glasses of the Snezhnaya merchants with Dawn Winery's own finest Dandelion Wine.

response.speaker: Vile
response.text: To show his respect, Master Diluc followed the Snezhnayan custom and downed the entire glass of Fire-Water.

response.speaker: Vile
response.text: The Snezhnayan guests then fervently applauded his heroism, and he nodded politely in response, but it wasn't long before he felt as if the world was spinning around him.

response.speaker: Vile
response.text: He managed to maintain his calm demeanor as owner of the winery to the end of the banquet. But once the festivities were over, Master Diluc lay passed out in his quarters for the next three days.

response.speaker: Vile
response.text: Everyone in Dawn Winery was worried if Master Diluc had actually fallen victim to some Snezhnayan plot.

response.speaker: Vile
response.text: Adelinde, who regularly tends to Master Diluc's daily needs, reassured everyone saying, "Master is fine. Although, I've never seen someone get drunk like that before..."

response.speaker: Vile
response.text: Once Master Diluc regained consciousness, the first thing he did was refuse the partnership with the Snezhnayan merchant — "The people of Mondstadt can't handle this."

choices.text: You should tell her about your concerns.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Seen anyone who looks a lot like me?

dialogues.speaker: Vile
dialogues.text: Oh, so you're looking for family.

dialogues.speaker: Vile
dialogues.text: While I know most anything about Mondstadt, I have to admit that this is one thing I'm not apprised of...

dialogues.speaker: Vile
dialogues.text: There's just been no time — too much on my plate, lately.

dialogues.speaker: Vile
dialogues.text: When I'm done settling those things, I'll help you look.
